To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inelastic nuclear interaction probability of high-energy pro-tons in a bent silicon crystal for the crystal orientation optimal in terms of the volume reflection was found to be a few percents higher than the probability of nuclear interactions for the amorph-ous case.
in the limiting quasi parallel beam case the inelastic nuclear interaction probability in a bent crystal decreases more than 5 times as compared to the amorphous silicon crystal.
in the limiting cases of quasi parallel and quasi perpendicular beams the nuclear losses in a bent crystal are 2–3 times smaller than in the amorphic case.

the development of the crystal collimators for the LHC.
a new approach to collimation of the LHC beam halo using a crystal.
the study of the nuclear interactions in bent crystals, which are the most important source of background for the collimation system of the Large Hadron Collider.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the probability of inelastic nuclear losses for the crystal orientation optimal to the volume reflection was a few percent larger than for the amorphously oriented crystal, but the probability for the quasi parallel beam was a factor of about 5 lower than for the collimated beam.
the probability of nuclear interactions for a bent crystal in the LHC conditions can be considered as a factor of about three smaller than the probability of the amorphous silicon.
a bent crystal is a good candidate for a primary collimator in a collider.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the probability of nuclear interactions in a bent crystal can be significantly smaller than in the amorphic material.
the probability of inelastic nuclear losses in the bent crystal is not much larger than in the case of an amorphous target.
the nuclear interaction probability in a short bent crystal is not much larger than in an amorphous absorber, which is an essential condition for the crystal as a primary absorber of the beam halo.
